_meta.description: Pre-parsed obligations of key APRA cross-industry prudential standards, extracted once from the authoritative APRA standards into structured form (the nist-ai-rmf-playbook / acsc-e8-maturity S3 pattern). Ingested deterministically via transport:s3 + mode:map — no live PDF fetch, no LLM extraction. Content faithful to the standards; re-parse to refresh on APRA updates.
_meta.source: APRA cross-industry prudential standards (CPS 220, CPS 230, CPS 234, CPS 511)
_meta.refresh: re-parse from apra.gov.au on standard revision

requirements.name: Maintain a risk management framework
requirements.description: An APRA-regulated institution must maintain a risk management framework (RMF) to manage the material risks to which it is exposed, appropriate to its size, business mix and complexity. The Board is ultimately responsible for the RMF and its oversight.

requirements.name: Board-approved risk appetite statement
requirements.description: The institution must have a risk appetite statement, approved by the Board, that articulates the degree of risk the institution is prepared to accept in pursuit of its objectives, including quantitative and qualitative measures.

requirements.name: Maintain a risk management strategy (RMS)
requirements.description: The institution must maintain a Board-approved risk management strategy that describes the RMF and how the institution's material risks are managed, and submit it to APRA.

requirements.name: Designated Chief Risk Officer
requirements.description: The institution must have a designated Chief Risk Officer (CRO) with sufficient seniority, authority and independence to oversee the risk management function, involved in all material risk decisions and with a direct reporting line to the CEO and access to the Board.

requirements.name: Board Risk Committee
requirements.description: The institution must have a Board Risk Committee to assist the Board in fulfilling its risk management oversight responsibilities.

requirements.name: Independent comprehensive review of the RMF
requirements.description: The institution must ensure a comprehensive review of the appropriateness, effectiveness and adequacy of the risk management framework is undertaken by operationally independent, appropriately trained and competent persons at least every three years.

requirements.name: Manage operational risk with effective controls
requirements.description: An APRA-regulated entity must manage its operational risks by maintaining appropriate internal controls and by monitoring their effectiveness, and must remediate identified weaknesses and incidents in a timely manner. (Effective 1 July 2025.)

requirements.name: Identify critical operations and set tolerance levels
requirements.description: The entity must identify its critical operations and establish tolerance levels for each — the maximum level of disruption it is willing to accept (e.g. maximum tolerable downtime, data loss). It must maintain a register of critical operations.

requirements.name: Maintain a business continuity plan
requirements.description: The entity must maintain a business continuity plan (BCP) setting out how it will maintain its critical operations within tolerance levels through disruptions, including credible options for responding to a range of severe disruptions.

requirements.name: Scenario analysis and annual BCP review
requirements.description: The entity must conduct scenario analysis to test its ability to continue to meet its tolerance levels for critical operations under a range of severe but plausible scenarios, and must review and test its BCP at least annually.

requirements.name: Manage material service providers
requirements.description: The entity must maintain a service provider management policy and a register of its material service providers (including fourth parties where relevant), manage the risks associated with those arrangements, and ensure agreements provide for APRA access. Consolidates the former CPS 231 Outsourcing and CPS 232 Business Continuity.

requirements.name: Notify APRA of material operational risk incidents
requirements.description: The entity must notify APRA as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of an operational risk incident that it determines to be likely to have a material financial impact or a material impact on its ability to maintain critical operations.

requirements.name: Maintain an information security capability
requirements.description: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain an information security capability commensurate with the size and extent of threats to its information assets, and which enables the continued sound operation of the entity.

requirements.name: Clearly define information security roles
requirements.description: The entity must clearly define the information-security-related roles and responsibilities of the Board, senior management, governing bodies and individuals.

requirements.name: Implement information security controls
requirements.description: The entity must implement controls to protect its information assets, including those managed by related parties and third parties, commensurate with the criticality and sensitivity of those assets, and must evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of controls.

requirements.name: Systematic testing of security controls
requirements.description: The entity must test the effectiveness of its information security controls through a systematic testing program, with the nature and frequency of testing commensurate with the rate of change of assets, threats, and the consequences of an incident; deficiencies must be escalated and remediated.

requirements.name: Internal audit review of information security
requirements.description: The entity's internal audit function must review the design and operating effectiveness of information security controls, including those maintained by related parties and third parties.

requirements.name: Notify APRA of information security incidents
requirements.description: The entity must notify APRA no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a material information security incident, and must notify APRA no later than 10 business days after becoming aware of a material information security control weakness it cannot remediate in a timely manner.

remuneration.title: Board-approved remuneration framework
remuneration.description: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain a remuneration framework, approved and overseen by the Board, that is designed to promote effective management of financial and non-financial risks, sustainable performance, and the long-term soundness of the entity. (Effective from 2023.)

remuneration.title: Board Remuneration Committee
remuneration.description: The entity must have a Board Remuneration Committee to oversee the design and operation of the remuneration framework, including remuneration outcomes for specified roles.

remuneration.title: Material weight on non-financial measures
remuneration.description: For significant financial institutions (SFIs), the variable remuneration of specified roles must give material weight to non-financial measures — including risk and conduct — with a minimum aggregate weighting of 40% on non-financial measures, so that remuneration is not driven predominantly by financial metrics.

remuneration.title: Deferral of variable remuneration
remuneration.description: For SFIs, a portion of variable remuneration for specified roles (e.g. senior managers and highly-paid material risk-takers) must be deferred over multi-year periods, with vesting aligned to the emergence of risk outcomes, so that pay reflects risk over time.

remuneration.title: Malus and clawback
remuneration.description: The entity must have the ability to apply downward adjustments (malus) to unvested deferred variable remuneration and, for SFIs, clawback of vested remuneration, where risk-management or conduct outcomes warrant, to ensure accountability for adverse outcomes.

remuneration.title: Remuneration reflects risk and conduct outcomes
remuneration.description: Remuneration outcomes must appropriately reflect risk-management and conduct outcomes, including the application of consequences for poor risk behaviour, breaches and misconduct.
